Fit Joint Species Distribution Models in mvgam

Source: R/jsdgam.R
jsdgam.Rd

Fits a joint species distribution model (JSDM) to the presences, detections or counts of many species across many sampling units. Species often co-occur more or less often than their responses to the measured covariates predict. A few latent factors capture that residual association. They need far fewer parameters than a full correlation matrix among species. The observation model takes the smooths, Gaussian processes and random effects of any mvgam model. The factors take their own predictors through factor_formula. Write lv_axis() in one of its terms to give each factor its own effect of a covariate, a constrained ordination.

Usage

jsdgam(
  formula,
  factor_formula = ~-1,
  knots,
  data,
  newdata,
  family = binomial(),
  unit = time,
  species = series,
  priors,
  n_lv = 2L,
  traits = NULL,
  trait_slopes = NULL,
  phylo = NULL,
  loadings_prior = NULL,
  backend = getOption("brms.backend", "cmdstanr"),
  threads = NULL,
  run_model = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

Main observation model formula (supports brms syntax). Smooth specials s(), t2(), gp(), varying intercepts and slopes, monotonic mo(), measurement-error me(), distributional dpar sub-formulas and offset() are all available. gp() accepts both the approximate Hilbert-space form (gp(x, k = 20)) and the exact full-covariance form (gp(x), no k). Prediction at newdata requires the approximate form. An exact gp() term fits and scores in-sample. mvgam() says so once per session.

factor_formula

A one-sided formula for the latent factors' linear predictor. Write lv_axis() in a term to give each factor its own effect, as in ~ s(elev, by = lv_axis()) or ~ elev:lv_axis(). Each covariate must take one value per sampling unit. The deprecated by = trend acts as by = lv_axis(). Defaults to ~ -1, factors without predictors.

knots

Optional named list of knot positions for smooth terms, by covariate, as knots of mvgam().

data

A data.frame or list holding the response, the covariates of both formulas, the unit column and the species factor.

Data held as arrays, as unmarked, ubms, flocker, Hmsc and spOccupancy take them, convert to this long format. pivot_detection_array() converts detection histories of occupancy and N-mixture data: [J, K], [N, J, K], multi-season [N, J, T, K] or a list of [J, K] matrices per species. pivot_species_matrix() converts a wide [J, N] species composition matrix.

newdata

Optional held-out data.frame, stored on the fit as object$test_data. Fitting draws no forecasts. forecast() called without newdata forecasts these times, carrying the fitted latent state forward. plot(fit, type = "series") overlays them. posterior_predict() on these data uses the covariate part alone. The section 'Which prediction function?' of predict.mvgam() compares the two.

family

The observation family every species shares, as a family object. mvgam_families lists them. Defaults to binomial() for presence-absence data. Counts take a count family such as poisson() or negbinomial().

For one family per species, write formula with one brms::bf() per species, each naming its family, as in bf(count ~ env, family = poisson()) + bf(seen ~ env, family = bernoulli()). The responses then form the species axis, in place of a species column. family applies to any response that names none.

The simplex families diri(), multi() and categ() need a per-species term, as in y ~ env * species or y ~ 0 + species + env:species. A coefficient shared by every species cancels from their likelihood. In y ~ env, b_Intercept and b_env take their priors alone. mvgam warns of this once per session. diri() sets out the identification.

unit

The unquoted name of the numeric column indexing the sampling units, often time or site. Defaults to time.

species

The unquoted name of the factor column indexing the species. Defaults to series, as in other mvgam models.

priors

Optional brmsprior of priors to set, from brms::prior(). prior, the brms spelling, is accepted in .... get_prior.mvgam_formula() lists the classes a model takes.

n_lv

Integer number of latent factors, from 1 to the number of species. Defaults to 2. The residual covariance Z Z' + diag(Psi^2) has rank at most the number of species. Further columns of Z add nothing.

Under the default Student-t prior on Z, or a structured prior built from traits, phylo or loadings_prior$distances, n_lv is the number of factors in the likelihood. Under the multiplicative gamma process prior (loadings_prior = "mgp" or list(column_shrinkage = "mgp", ...)) it is a ceiling. The prior shrinks later columns towards zero. A larger loadings_prior$mgp_a2 shrinks them harder. active_factors() counts the factors the data support.

traits

Optional species traits for a structured loadings prior: a data.frame or matrix with one row per species, or the name of an element of data2. Rows are matched to levels(data[[species]]) by a series column, by row name or by order. Factor columns are one-hot encoded and numeric columns are standardised. They become loadings_prior$features. Supplying an explicit loadings_prior as well is refused.

trait_slopes

Optional one-sided formula of traits, such as ~ trait1 + trait2, for trait-mediated responses to the environment (the fourth-corner model of Hmsc). Each population-level term of formula becomes a non-linear parameter regressed on the traits, plus a species-level deviation. The deviations of intercept and slope correlate under an LKJ prior ((1 | sp | species)). The traits must be columns of data, constant within species. A smooth of a trait goes in trait_slopes, as ~ s(trait1). A smooth in formula is refused, because brms's top-level non-linear formula takes none. The defaults are std_normal() on each trait coefficient and student_t(3, 0, 2.5) on the species SD. priors overrides them.

phylo

Optional phylogeny: an ape::phylo tree, whose cophenetic distances are taken, or a numeric distance matrix with row and column names matching levels(data[[species]]). The distances are rescaled to a maximum of 1 and become loadings_prior$distances$phylo. A tree that is not ultrametric draws a warning once. A tree requires the ape package. Supplying an explicit loadings_prior as well is refused.

loadings_prior

Optional structured prior on the loadings, as loadings_prior of mvgam() takes it. Supplying traits or phylo as well is refused.

backend

"cmdstanr" or "rstan". Defaults to getOption("brms.backend", "cmdstanr").

threads

Positive integer number of threads per chain, or NULL (the default) for none. The model is compiled with cpp_options$stan_threads = TRUE. cmdstanr then samples with threads_per_chain = threads. The closure-unit families (nmix(), occ()) and the multi-response families (diri(), mvn(), mvt(), multi(), categ()) split their likelihood over units with reduce_sum, in about eight chunks. With 50 or more closure units, threads = 4 samples about a third faster. Fewer units can sample slower, the threading overhead outweighing the gain. A brms family without a trend_formula uses the threading brms writes.

A brms family with a trend_formula samples each chain on one thread whatever threads says. The threaded likelihood brms writes leaves no place to add the trend. Each such fit warns.

run_model

Logical. FALSE builds the model without parsing, compiling or sampling it. The result holds $stancode, $standata and the prior table, with $fit set to NULL. stancode.mvgam_formula(), standata.mvgam_formula() and get_prior.mvgam_formula() return them. Methods that need draws, such as summary() and forecast(), refuse it. A jsdgam() model has no mvgam_formula(), which makes run_model = FALSE the way to inspect one before fitting. Defaults to TRUE.

...

Further arguments of mvgam(), such as data2 (where traits and phylo find a named element), algorithm, chains and silent.

Value

A fitted model of class c("mvgam", "jsdgam", "brmsfit"). Every mvgam method applies, such as summary(), predict(), forecast() and loo(). ordinate() and residual_cor() describe the factors. update(fit, n_lv = 3) refits it through jsdgam() with the arguments given changed.

References

Warton, D. I., Blanchet, F. G., O'Hara, R. B., Ovaskainen, O., Taskinen, S., Walker, S. C. and Hui, F. K. C. (2015). So many variables: joint modeling in community ecology. Trends in Ecology and Evolution, 30(12):766-779. doi:10.1016/j.tree.2015.09.007

Ovaskainen, O., Tikhonov, G., Norberg, A., Blanchet, F. G., Duan, L., Dunson, D., Roslin, T. and Abrego, N. (2017). How to make more out of community data? Ecology Letters, 20(5):561-576. doi:10.1111/ele.12757

Tikhonov, G., Opedal, O. H., Abrego, N., Lehikoinen, A., de Jonge, M. M. J., Oksanen, J. and Ovaskainen, O. (2020). Joint species distribution modelling with the R-package Hmsc. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 11(3):442-447. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13345

Hui, F. K. C. (2016). boral - Bayesian Ordination and Regression Analysis of Multivariate Abundance Data in R. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7(6):744-750. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12514

Heaps, S. E. and Jermyn, I. H. (2024). Structured prior distributions for the covariance matrix in latent factor models. Statistics and Computing, 34:143. doi:10.1007/s11222-024-10454-0

See also

sim_jsdgam() simulates data this function fits. sim_closure_unit_data() simulates the occ() and nmix() case. residual_cor(), ordinate(), shared_variation(), active_factors() and compare_loadings() interpret the fitted factors. lv_axis() gives each factor its own covariate effect. how_to_cite() drafts a methods paragraph for the fit and methods_md() writes its equations. The JSDM article fits a negative binomial model with a trait-informed loadings prior, ordination biplots and multiplicative gamma process shrinkage.

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_formula(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula(), update.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Detections of 6 species at 80 sites, 4 visits each. Occupancy
# responds to the site covariate `env` and detection to the time of
# day `tod_c`. Two latent factors drive the species associations.
simdat <- sim_closure_unit_data(
  family    = occ(),
  n_species = 6L,
  n_sites   = 80L,
  n_visits  = 4L,
  n_lv      = 2L,
  seed      = 1L
)

# A joint occupancy model. Each species has its own occupancy
# intercept and `env` slope, plus its own detection intercept. Two
# latent factors take up the residual association.
mod <- jsdgam(
  formula        = bf(y ~ series * env, p ~ series + tod_c),
  factor_formula = ~ -1,
  data           = simdat$data_train,
  family         = occ(),
  n_lv           = 2L,
  chains         = 2,
  silent         = 2
)
#> Warning: 210 of 2000 (10.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

summary(mod)

# The effect of `env` on the chance of a detection, occupancy times
# detection
conditional_effects(mod)





# The residual correlations among species the factors imply
plot(residual_cor(mod))


# Site scores and species loadings on the two factors
ordinate(mod, rotation = "varimax")
